title: Michoacán
capsule: The Tarascan state (P'urhépecha: Iréchecua Tzintzuntzani), centered on Lake Pátzcuaro with its capital at Tzintzuntzan, was the dominant polity of western Mexico and the only major Mesoamerican state never subjugated by the Aztec Triple Alliance. It expanded rapidly under Tariacuri (r. c. 1320–1350) and his nephews; under Zuangua (d. 1520) the empire repelled every Aztec incursion and no Aztec army defeated Tarascan forces in the field. The state was noted for advanced copper metallurgy and distinctive stepped rectangular yácatas. In 1522 the last cazonci, Tangaxuan II, submitted peacefully to the conquistador Cristóbal de Olid, but was tortured and executed on the orders of Nuño de Guzmán in 1530, completing violent Spanish subjugation.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory of the Tarascan state around Lake Pátzcuaro is well established archaeologically and from early colonial sources; the outer limits of the empire's tributary reach are estimated from conquest records and are moderately well mapped.
